en: Taal Volcano features Vulcan Point, an island located inside a crater lake that sits on a larger island inside Taal Lake.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River flows directly into the sea, meaning its lower portion experiences ocean tides.
The peak of Mount Pulag frequently drops below freezing, making it one of the few Philippine locations to experience frost.
The Philippine Trench reaches a depth of over 10,500 meters, making it the third deepest oceanic trench globally.
The Philippine eagle, endemic to Mindanao, has a unique shaggy crest and is one of the largest eagles globally.
The Agusan Marsh in Mindanao is the largest wetland in the Philippines, acting as a massive natural sponge for floodwaters.
Tinuy-an Falls in Surigao del Sur is nicknamed the 'Niagara of the Philippines' because of its wide, multi-tiered curtain flow.
The province of Batanes consists of ten inhabited islands located just 190 kilometers south of the island of Taiwan.
Callao Cave in Cagayan contains a massive natural skylight that illuminates its main chamber with a stunning, direct sunbeam.
Lake Sebu in South Cotabato is uniquely composed of seven distinct lakes connected by a network of natural waterfalls.
The Philippines is the second-largest nickel producer in the world, primarily mining the mineral from laterite soils in Surigao.
The island of Luzon is so massive that it ranks as the fifteenth largest island in the entire world.
